subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: Brave New World and Engineered Society
description: A short lesson to help you apply Brave New World and Engineered Society.

hook.text: Aldous Huxley imagined a future where people were not oppressed by force but controlled through pleasure.

buildup.text: Brave New World described a society where humans were grown in labs and drugged into permanent happiness.

discovery.text: Published in 1932, it predicted genetic engineering, mood-altering drugs, and entertainment as control.

twist.text: Unlike Orwell's boot on the face, Huxley warned that people would voluntarily surrender their freedom.

climax.text: Many argue Huxley's vision came closer to reality than Orwell's, as we chose distraction over awareness.

punchline.text: The scariest prison is one people choose to enter.

quiz.question: How does Brave New World differ from Nineteen Eighty-Four?
options: It portrays control through pleasure, not force
It takes place in the past instead of the future
It focuses on a single character's diary
